original_value: SummaryNanometer CMOS technologies are characterized by low intrinsic gain and limited rejection to common‐mode disturbances, issues that analog designers must counteract through nonconventional circuit solutions able to operate under sub–1‐V supply voltages. In this letter, an approach originally proposed as a common‐mode control loop for body‐driven amplifiers is exploited by cross‐connecting the bulk terminals of the active‐load transistors of a source‐coupled pair to sensibly improve its small‐signal performance. A design example in 65‐nm process supplied from 750 mV shows that the presented solution offers both a nominal 20‐dB increase in differential gain and 29‐dB increase in CMRR, as compared with the standard counterpart.

result.paraphrase: Summary Nanometer CMOS technologies exhibit low intrinsic gain and poor common-mode disturbance rejection, forcing analog designers to use unconventional circuit techniques that can function below 1 V supply levels. In this letter, a method first introduced as a common-mode control loop for body-driven amplifiers is applied by cross-connecting the bulk terminals of the active-load transistors in a source-coupled pair, noticeably enhancing small-signal performance. A 65 nm design example powered at 750 mV shows that the proposed solution provides a nominal 20 dB gain increase in differential gain and a 29 dB improvement in CMRR versus the standard version.
